requirement_text.REQ-067: Port src/api/pagination.zig (406 lines, R-Co's API-06) as Letflow.Api.Pagination -- the shared cursor encode/decode, prefix validation, expiry checking, page-size validation, and standardised page response that every S4 list endpoint delegates to. Port the constants exactly: MAX_PAGE_SIZE 200, DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE 50, MIN_PAGE_SIZE 1, CURSOR_EXPIRY_US 86_400_000_000. A requested page size above MAX_PAGE_SIZE, below MIN_PAGE_SIZE, or non-numeric is a 400, not a silent clamp. A cursor carries a type prefix so a cursor minted by one endpoint cannot be replayed against another. An expired cursor is rejected. SECURITY (INV-1, INV-5): the decoded cursor struct must have no tenant/schema field -- tenant scoping comes exclusively from REQ-072's future resolved request context, never from the cursor. A cursor minted in tenant A and replayed against tenant B must return tenant B's page or an error, never tenant A's rows. Paging through more rows than one page holds must return every row exactly once with no duplicate and no gap across at least three successive pages.

task.description:
Write `test/specs/REQ-067.md` and `test/letflow/api/pagination_test.exs` for `Letflow.Api.Pagination`, gated PASS through design/security/idiom review. Every one of REQ-067's six acceptance criteria needs at least one test case that would genuinely fail if the property were violated.

SPECIFIC CASES TO COVER, per the acceptance criteria:
1. Constants: assert `max_page_size/0`==200, `default_page_size/0`==50, `min_page_size/0`==1, `cursor_expiry_us/0`==86_400_000_000 -- against the accessor functions, not hardcoded literals duplicated in the test.
2. Page-size validation: 201 -> rejected; 0 -> rejected; a non-numeric string (e.g. `"abc"`) -> rejected at the `parse_page_size_param/1` layer (per the design's split). Also cover the boundary values (1, 200) succeeding and `nil` returning the default.
3. Cross-endpoint prefix rejection: build a cursor with one prefix (e.g. `"T:"`), attempt to decode it with a different prefix (e.g. `"I:"`), assert rejection.
4. Expiry: construct a cursor whose embedded timestamp is deliberately old (do NOT wait in real time -- build the raw cursor string directly with an old timestamp value), decode with a short `expiry_window_us`, assert rejection. Also cover a cursor that is NOT expired succeeding.
5. INV-1 (tenant isolation): this is the security-load-bearing test. Write a test that (a) confirms by inspection/reflection that `Cursor`'s struct fields are exactly `[:inner]` -- e.g. `Map.from_struct(cursor) |> Map.keys()` or `%Letflow.Api.Pagination.Cursor{} |> Map.from_struct() |> Map.keys()` equals `[:inner]` -- and (b) constructs a minimal FIXTURE store function (a plain Elixir function in the test file, not real app code) that takes a tenant id and a decoded cursor and simulates 'this endpoint's own scoping', demonstrating that a cursor minted while iterating tenant A's data, when decoded and handed to a lookup scoped to tenant B, returns tenant B's rows (or an error) and never tenant A's -- because the cursor itself carries no tenant information for the lookup to accidentally honour.
6. Pagination completeness: build a raw in-memory list of >2 pages' worth of items (using `build_raw_cursor/3`/`build_raw_cursor_timestamp_key/4` to construct the cursor chain), page through it via three or more successive calls, and assert every item appears exactly once, no duplicates, no gaps.

Also cover: `encode_cursor/1`/`decode_cursor/4` round-trip; `parse_int_from_cursor/3` and `find_nth_colon/2`'s own edge cases (out-of-bounds offset, no colon found); `build_raw_cursor/3` and `build_raw_cursor_timestamp_key/4`'s exact output format.

Self-sufficient, deterministic tests: no wall-clock waiting, no shared/hardcoded test data across cases, no dependency on test execution order.

Mix is at `/c/Program Files/Elixir/bin/mix` if not on PATH. Complete your work synchronously within this turn per `core-directives.md`'s rule. Do NOT run the suite yet if that would be a separate step -- but per WF-02, you may compile-check your own test file.
acceptance_criteria: Every one of REQ-067's six acceptance criteria has at least one test case that would fail if the property were violated
test/specs/REQ-067.md is written alongside the test code, stating why each test case exists
The INV-1 test demonstrates the tenant-isolation property concretely, including confirming the Cursor struct's field set by inspection
The expiry test constructs an old cursor directly rather than waiting on wall-clock time
No test depends on unseeded randomness, shared hardcoded IDs across tests, or execution order
